Divergence 1.5.1 (83)

  • Pairing is easier to find. The paste-a-code field is now on the Sharing tab directly, next to “Copy pairing code”, instead of hidden behind a disclosure at the bottom. Copy on one computer, paste on the other. Sending the key as a file still works and sits just below.
  • A new account is told what to do next. Signing in for the first time showed two empty lists and nothing else. It now explains that an empty list is expected, and walks through installing Divergence on the other computer, sharing the pairing code, and granting the permissions a Mac needs in order to be viewed.

Divergence 1.5.1 (82)

  • Your Mac stays reachable more consistently. It was briefly dropping and re-establishing its connection to the relay around thirty times an hour, reacting to network changes that did not actually affect it — and during each gap another machine trying to reach it would be told it was offline. It now checks whether anything really changed first.
  • Disconnections say why they happened. When a session ended, the log recorded it as user-initiated no matter what actually caused it. It now names the real reason, which makes a dropped session something we can diagnose from a log rather than guess at.

Divergence 1.5.1 (81)

  • Macs can connect to each other again. A secure connection between two Macs could fail every time, reporting the other machine as offline or not paired when it was neither. Both machines were identifying themselves correctly — Divergence was comparing the two forms of the same identifier as though they were different machines.
  • If one Mac is updated and the other is not, connections between them start working again as soon as either side is on this version.
